steps.text: Whisk lime juice, tequila, orange juice, cilantro, chiles, chili powder, honey, garlic, salt, and pepper together in a bowl; pour into a 1-gallon resealable bag. Add pork tenderloins, coat with marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for 8 hours.
When ready to cook, preheat an outdoor grill for high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Remove tenderloins from marinade and shake off excess. Discard remaining marinade.
Cook tenderloins on the preheated grill, turning occasionally, until meat has reached an internal temperature of 145 degrees F (63 degrees C), about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Tequila Lime Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: Grilled tequila-lime pork tenderloin is marinated overnight, then grilled until tender. This recipe makes two tenderloins, but you can freeze one to make later.
raw_recipe.name: Tequila Lime Pork Tenderloin

review.reviewBody: Used a meat tenderizer to poke holes in the meat and then marinated for about 4 hours. While the meat cooked on the grill, I cooked down the marinade and added a cornstarch slurry to make a nice sauce. Totally full of flavor and pretty darn healthy for you, too. We enjoyed this and will be making again.

I took a large pork loin and split it into two halves and cut them each in half. I also doubled the marinade and marinated the meat 4 hours, then cooked down the marinade to thicken it. On a charcoal grille, I got the coals good and hot and sprinkled apple wood chips over the top, then quickly added the meat and closed the lid and vents. That creates a heavy smoke. After twenty minutes, l opened the lid and turned the meat. Using the grille lid and vents, I kept the temp at around 275 and cooked the meat for an hour, turning it often and basting it with the cooked down marinade. It was a hit.

I made it with a little more Tequila than recipe,and maranated it overnight.. !!!! I slow cooked it in an oven bag, in a crock pot, and it came out so very tender!!! Everyone in the family agreed on the 5 stars!!!!

Second (third really) time making this grilled pork tenderloin. First try didn't impress, but I saved the 2nd pork loin in the freezer with marinade for about 3 months before grilling it. That really helps the flavor, plus reducing the marinade to use as a dipping sauce as others suggest helps add even more flavor if you overcook the meat a little. 3rd time I let the pork marinate for 48 hours and it came out great. Even with high temp grilling, you can really taste the lime and other ingredients if you let it marinate long enough. Got the 2nd loin in the freezer, ready to cook in a month or so.

This is a great recipe, it’s good with tenderloin, but try doubling the orange juice, and then having ham steaks marinade in it. We did this for Christmas, and it was incredible. Then we took the marinade, boiled it down on the stove and made a sauce for the ham. It was delicious. A favorite already!!
Instead of grilling, I cubed the pork and after browning it, simmered in skillet with marinade until it was done and the marinade absorbed. Very flavorful.

i didn't have tequila and kept it rather mild, but my goodness was this good! It was also middle of winter so I seared it on both sides and then cooked it in a 400 degree oven for 30 minutes, or until it was 160 degrees.

Great for pork fajitas. I marinated pork loin after cutting into fajita-size pieces. Only had time to marinate for an hour, then sautéed stovetop with a little olive oil. I didn't have cilantro, but the flavors were great anyway.
So I'm Chicago middle of January couldn't use a grill. We conveniently Baked it till it hit 125 degrees then switched it to broil till 145. So juicy

I used this marinade in a grill-off with my dad and it gave me the win! I added a little bit extra of everything and soaked a whole pork loin overnight. I grilled the pork loin over indirect heat for a nice and slow cook. I also basted the pork loin with some extra marinade while it cooked. It was delicious and added great flavor. It also browned beautifully over the meat.

This marinade was fantastic and had great flavour! I think the key to the flavour not being lost is to slice the tenderlion into 1 inch medallions before putting it in the marinade. I only used 1/2 the recipe and there was plenty of marinade to coat all the meat in a large bag. If you slice your pork (or chicken would be great to)o, I would only marinade for 3-5 hours since the lime and orange slightly cooks the meat. Cook the medallions on medium heat 3-4 minutes per side or until the internal temperature reaches 155 degrees F and let it rest for 5 minutes to reach a final 160 degrees F. I did a rough chop of the meat and served in corn tortillas for a mexican dinner.
Was very good. I let it marinate overnight. Next time pour some of the sauce (after boiling it)) over the tenderloin before serving it.
Pork came out tender and juicy, but unfortunately, I didn't care for the flavor at all. Will not make again.
Try OK

I made this pork tenderloin as shown in the recipe. Unfortunately life got in the way and it wound up sitting in the marinade for over 18 hours before I had a chance to get it on the grill. The result was a perfectly cooked pork loin with an unbelievably strong lime taste. Next time I make it I will make sure it marinates no more then 8 hour.
This recipe is a keeper. However I plan to reduce the amount of chili powder next time I make it as it was a bit overbearing. The pork was moist and tender.
Made it. Loved it! Didn’t have the cilantro or chilies, but nonetheless the pork was delicious. Served it with roasted potatoes and corn.

Really disappointing. I poked holes in my tenderloins and marinated for over a day, and the flavor still just wasn't there. It wasn't bad, but it didn't taste like lime or tequila, and I can think of a few better things to make with those.
Very easy to grill but needed gravy sauce
Great marinade. Sliced the tenderloin into medallions and then marinated. Took about 10 minutes on bbq
